title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 38 (Punishment for Personation for Acquisition, etc., of Securities)

content.overview: Section 38 punishes any person who makes or abets an application in a fictitious name for acquiring or subscribing for securities, or makes or abets multiple applications in different names or combinations, or otherwise induces a company to allot or register transfer of securities in a fictitious name. Liability is under section 447. The court may also order disgorgement of securities and other prescribed consequences.
content.glance: Fictitious-name applications; multiple applications in different names; inducing allotment/transfer to a fictitious name; s. 447; possible disgorgement.
content.study: Any person who (a) makes or abets making of an application in a fictitious name to a company for acquiring, or subscribing for, its securities, or (b) makes or abets making of multiple applications to a company in different names or in different combinations of names for acquiring or subscribing for its securities, or (c) otherwise induces directly or indirectly a company to allot, or register any transfer of, securities to him or any other person in a fictitious name, is liable under section 447. Where a person has been convicted, the court may also order that any securities allotted be transferred to the company or sold and proceeds forfeited as prescribed. Current-law framing: identify the form of personation (fictitious name, multiple names, or inducement); apply s. 447; note possible court orders on securities.

sections.heading: Fictitious-Name Application
sections.body: Making or abetting an application in a fictitious name for acquiring or subscribing for securities.

sections.heading: Multiple Applications
sections.body: Making or abetting multiple applications in different names or combinations of names.

sections.heading: Inducement of Allotment/Transfer
sections.body: Otherwise inducing the company to allot or register transfer of securities in a fictitious name.

sections.heading: Consequence
sections.body: Liability under section 447; court may order transfer or sale of allotted securities as prescribed.

provisions.title: Punishment for personation for acquisition, etc., of securities

examples.title: Fictitious name application
examples.body: A person applies for IPO shares in a false name. Section 38 engages s. 447 liability.

examples.title: Multiple applications
examples.body: The same person submits several applications under different names to obtain a larger allotment. Section 38 is engaged.

hypotheticals.question: Is using a relative’s genuine name with consent still personation under s. 38?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 38 targets fictitious names and multiple applications in different names/combinations; genuine applications by different real persons are outside the personation rule, but multiple applications by the same person in different names fall within it.

distinctions.title: Personation (s. 38) vs fraudulent inducement (s. 36)
distinctions.left: Fictitious identity or multiple applications to obtain securities
distinctions.right: False statements/concealment to induce investment agreements

misconceptions.trap: Only the company can complain of personation.
misconceptions.correction: Section 38 creates criminal liability under s. 447 for the specified personation conduct; prosecution is not limited to a company complaint in the statutory text.

cases.name: Salomon v. A. Salomon & Co. Ltd.
cases.facts: Properly incorporated company challenged as indistinct from controller.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Registered company is a separate legal person.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 38 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify form of personation (a)/(b)/(c). II. Apply s. 447. III. Note possible orders on securities. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Conduct type; evidence of fictitious name/multiple applications/inducement; s. 447; disgorgement if relevant.
